Def.Content: still, yet: up to now, up to a specific point in the past.

Examples.Phrase: Natúlug pa si Pidru,
Examples.Gloss: Pedro is still asleep.

Examples.Phrase: Si Huwan pay naabut,
Examples.Gloss: So far only John has arrived.

Def.Content: with measurements: only [so-and-so much] up to now.

Examples.Phrase: Tungà pa ug túbig ang baril,
Examples.Gloss: The barrel is still only half full of water.

Def.Content: not yet.

Examples.Phrase: Ang linung-ag nga ságing walà pa malútù,
Examples.Gloss: The boiled bananas are not cooked yet.

Def.Content: before.

Examples.Phrase: Hipúsa ang libru sa dílì pa si Pápa muabut,
Examples.Gloss: Put the book away before Dad arrives.

Examples.Phrase: Sa wà pay gíra,
Examples.Gloss: Before the war.

Def.Content: else, in addition.
with future verb: [so-and-so] will still happen.

Examples.Phrase: Sulatan pa nákù si Husi,
Examples.Gloss: I still have to write to José.

Def.Content: with a past verb: [did] besides.

Examples.Phrase: Human siya sagpáa, gisultían pa ug pait,
Examples.Gloss: He was slapped and bitter words were said to him as well.

Def.Content: with existential: [so-and-so] also is in existence.

Examples.Phrase: Náa pa bay túbig sa baril?
Examples.Gloss: Is there any more water in the barrel?

Def.Content: interrogative —:
what, where, why, etc. else.

Examples.Phrase: Kinsa pay muadtu?
Examples.Gloss: Who else will go?

Def.Content: what, where, why, etc. could it be.

Examples.Phrase: Unsa pa ug dílì kwarta?
Examples.Gloss: What could it be <corr id="xd20e323227" title="Source: it">if</corr> not money?

Examples.Phrase: Ngánu pa nga ikaw giyud?
Examples.Gloss: Why, oh why, was it you, of all people?

Def.Content: [noun]-un what [noun] are you talking about?

Examples.Phrase: Unsa pay radiyúhun nga dúgay nang gikáwat,
Examples.Gloss: What radio are you talking about when it was stolen long ago.

Def.Content: in phrases bringing up a new subject:
by the way, to change the subject.

Examples.Phrase: Láin pay átù, minyù ka na ba?
Examples.Gloss: By the way, are you married?

Def.Content: by the way, I just thought of it.

Examples.Phrase: Mau pa diay átù, wà ta kadág abridur,
Examples.Gloss: It just occurred to me. We didn’t bring a can opener.

Def.Content: excuse me a second (lit. one more second).

Examples.Phrase: ísà pa kay ákung pagngun ang radiyu,
Examples.Gloss: Excuse me. I am going to turn off the radio.

Def.Content: in phrases meaning in addition:
even ... too, despite.

Examples.Phrase: Bísan pa ang mga bátà giapil,
Examples.Gloss: Even the children were included.

Examples.Phrase: Bísan pa niánà, dì ku muadtu,
Examples.Gloss: Despite that, I won’t go!

Def.Content: besides.

Examples.Phrase: Gawas (lábut) pa niánà, unsa pa may púlung níya?
Examples.Gloss: Besides that, what else did he say?

Def.Content: in addition to.

Examples.Phrase: Labaw pa niánà tagáan tikag primiyu,
Examples.Gloss: And in addition, I will give you a reward.

Def.Content: [predicate] is <corr id="xd20e323305" title="Source: superflous">superfluous</corr>; [do] when one shouldn’t or shouldn’t have to.

Examples.Phrase: Ug nagbayadbáyad pa siya nga wà man tu kinahanglána,
Examples.Gloss: And he was paying for it when there was no need.

Examples.Phrase: Sus! Ipakítà pa giyud níya mu rag dílì baratuhun,
Examples.Gloss: Heavens! She has to show off, as if it weren’t s.t. cheap.

Def.Content: [do] some more so that [such-and-such] a bad thing will happen again.

Examples.Phrase: Nasagpaan ka. Panabì pa,
Examples.Gloss: You got yourself a slapping. Go on. Blabber some more.

Examples.Phrase: Nadagmà ka núun. Sígi, dágan pa,
Examples.Gloss: You fell down. Go on. Keep on running around (so you can fall again).

Def.Content: that’s what happens when you do [so-and-so].

Examples.Phrase: Minyù pa. Mu ra na kag irung panit,
Examples.Gloss: That is what you get for getting married. You’re no better off than a mangy dog.

Def.Content: [doubled verb] — didn’t even do [so-and-so] though it is customary.

Examples.Phrase: Gipalit níya ang kutsi dihàdihà nga wà nay hangyùhangyù pa,
Examples.Gloss: He bought the car, then and there, without even bargaining.

Def.Content: [so-and-so] was the case, which was bad enough, but then ...

Examples.Phrase: Mau pay kisì, ímu pung iuran ug sígi, nadúnut,
Examples.Gloss: It was already torn. You kept wearing it, so it was ruined.

Def.Content: he [did, does] and yet dared, dares to do [so-and-so] in addition.

Examples.Phrase: Mau pay sad-an mau pay mangísug,
Examples.Gloss: He is at fault, but he dares to get mad.

Examples.Phrase: Mau pay nangáyù mau pay mipílì,
Examples.Gloss: He is asking the favor and yet he is choosy.

Def.Content: [subject] is still in a group with other things mentioned.

Examples.Phrase: Ang íhu isdà. Isdà pa ba ang pági?
Examples.Gloss: Sharks are fish; are rays also considered fish?

Def.Content: that’s not so bad, is it?

Examples.Phrase: Sígi málu pa nà ug makadiyis ka,
Examples.Gloss: Go ahead. If you make ten bucks on it, that ain’t bad.

Def.Content: in comparisons: even more.

Examples.Phrase: Gwápa pa ka kang Maríya,
Examples.Gloss: You are more beautiful than Mary.

Def.Content: [subject] is more [adj.] than ...

Examples.Phrase: Lamì pay lamaw niíni,
Examples.Gloss: This is worse than garbage. (Lit. Garbage is more delicious than this.)

Examples.Phrase: Lisud pay magkaug mani,
Examples.Gloss: It’s harder to eat peanuts than do this.

Def.Content: in quotations, preceded by gen.: [gen.] said.

Examples.Phrase: Ug mau tu ang nahitabù, níya pa,
Examples.Gloss: And that is all what happened, he said.

Def.Content: [gen.] [gen.] says, said.

Examples.Phrase: Mátud pa níla aku dílì ángay,
Examples.Gloss: They say I am not worthy.

Def.Content: he said.

Examples.Phrase: Kay na, siya pa, unsáun man nákù?
Examples.Gloss: Well, said he, what can I do?

Def.Content: in other words.

Examples.Phrase: Aw, sa átù pa diyis ákung ibáyad nímu,
Examples.Gloss: Oh, in other words, ten is what I pay you.

Def.Content: with the apodosis of a condition contrary to fact.

Examples.Phrase: Ug walà pa nímu kawáta, ngánung náa man nà nímu?
Examples.Gloss: If you hadn’t stolen it, why do you have it?

Examples.Phrase: noun, pronoun, adj.
Examples.Gloss: ] if [noun] were [noun, pronoun, adj.].

Examples.Phrase: Aku pay Huwan,
Examples.Gloss: If I were John.

Examples.Phrase: Aku pay ikaw (aku pa nímu),
Examples.Gloss: If I were you.

Examples.Phrase: Aku pay dátù,
Examples.Gloss: If I were rich.

Examples.Phrase: Aku pa nímu, níya,
Examples.Gloss: If I were you, him.

Examples.Phrase: Kami pa ninyu, níla,
Examples.Gloss: If we were you, them.

Def.Content: ! [so-and-so] is stupendous in quantity, quality (lit. if you could only see [such-and-such]).

Examples.Phrase: Mais pay ímu, sus kadaghan!
Examples.Gloss: If you could only see my corn. My! There’s a lot.

Examples.Phrase: Si Pidru pay ímu, káun giyud tug irù,
Examples.Gloss: Believe me, Pedro will eat dog meat, and how!

Def.Content: I never thought [so-and-so] was what he was.

Examples.Phrase: Si Pidru pay ákù may kirída diay nà siya,
Examples.Gloss: I never thought it was possible, but Pedro has a mistress.

Def.Content: lámang: 4b, c.
it would be, would have been better if, it would have been good.

Examples.Phrase: Maáyu (agad) pa untà ug átung napintálan ang kahun úsà gawía,
Examples.Gloss: It would have been better if we had painted the box before we used it.

Examples.Phrase: Agad (maáyu) pa ug magtuun ka kay sa magkantakanta,
Examples.Gloss: You would do better to study than just sit around singing.

Def.Content: I hope that.

Examples.Phrase: Hináut pang dílì muulan,
Examples.Gloss: I hope it won’t rain.

Def.Content: modifying a phrase referring to time: [so-and-so] recently happened, won’t happen until ...

Examples.Phrase: Dílì madala ug bálik ugmà, Huybis pa,
Examples.Gloss: I cannot bring it back tomorrow. Not until Thursday.

Examples.Phrase: Bag-u pa siya nga milakaw,
Examples.Gloss: He left just now.

Examples.Phrase: Gíkan pa siya sa Manílà,
Examples.Gloss: He is just back from Manila.

Examples.Phrase: Karun pa siya muabut gíkan sa Buhul,
Examples.Gloss: He arrived just now from Bohol.

Def.Content: only then [will so-and-so] happen.

Examples.Phrase: Ayhà (anhà) pa siya mulíhuk ug pakit-an ug latigu,
Examples.Gloss: He only moves if he sees a whip.

Def.Content: only then [so-and-so] happened.

Examples.Phrase: Dihà pa siya mutuun nga hápit na ang iksámin,
Examples.Gloss: He only started to study when it was nearly exam time.

Def.Content: that is the first time [abstract] happened, [instrumental passive] will happen.

Examples.Phrase: Mau pay pagkadungug nákù niánà,
Examples.Gloss: That is the first time I heard that.

Examples.Phrase: Mau pay ilung-ag ug mudtu na,
Examples.Gloss: Don’t cook it until noon. (The first time to cook it when it’s noon.)

Def.Content: but then when [so-and-so] was done.

Examples.Phrase: Dúgay nákung limpiyu sa salug. Baldiyúhan pa nákù, human dáyun,
Examples.Gloss: It took me a long time to clean the floor. But then when I hosed it down, it was finished right away.

Examples.Phrase: Pag-abri pa nákù sa subri, wà diay sulud,
Examples.Gloss: When I opened the envelope, there was nothing in it after all.

Def.Content: knew [so-and-so] in advance.

Examples.Phrase: Dáan pa lagi ku,
Examples.Gloss: I knew that long ago!

Def.Content: much less [do].

Examples.Phrase: Dì gánì aku makasulti, kanta pa,
Examples.Gloss: I cannot even talk, much less sing.

Examples.Phrase: Dì gánì aku makahímù niánà, ikaw pa,
Examples.Gloss: I can’t even do that, much less you.
